newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore HSFO up on crude gains, fewer supplies.
newsitem.headline: Singapore HSFO up on crude gains, fewer supplies.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil prices on Wednesday were expected to move higher on crude gains, traders said.

Traders were however mixed on near term market direction. While some traders said supplies in the region are gradually being sold out and availabilities diminishing, others said supplies were adequate to meet demand.
The former said there were less Mideast cargoes seen heading east in late November/early December while Chinese demand was on the rise.
News of a possible oil export strike at Kuwait's Mina Al-Ahmadi refinery terminal have also firmed sentiment.
The strike, by Kuwaiti oil worker's union, was being considered over a dispute with Kuwait National Petroleum Company over its promotion system.
South Korean supplies were also capped as LG-Caltex's Oil Corp has delayed starting up a 220,000 barrels per day crude unit on November 23 after finding a defect in its topper's column.

A Dutch trader who was a seller last week has turned buyer, traders said. 180-centistoke fuel oil was bid at $118.50 per tonne for December, free-on-board Singapore, up 50 cents from Tuesday's quotes.
SIMEX fuel oil futures traded at $119.00 per tonne for December, up 50 cents from its previous close, with 10 lots traded.
December swaps traded at $118.00/$119.00, firm from Tuesday's $117.75/$118.50.
